newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes up on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes up on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up 155 basis points at 31.25 percent on Monday as liquidity was drained ahead of Wednesday's cutoff date for banks to settle outstanding balances on checking accounts with the central bank, trader said.
"The cutoff date is coming and dealers are picking up liquidity ahead of time. They're getting ready," said a trader.
Traders noted, however, that volume and dealing were light as in many recent sessions.
Dealers also noted that expected gains in primary interest rates at Tuesday's auction were also partly responsible for the gain in secondary rates.
Overnight rates meanwhile closed up 125 basis points at 32.00 percent, alos due to liquidity shortages.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 2.149 billion pesos by auctioning two credits which it assigned at 31.78 and 31.86 percent.
Dealers said government spending off some three billion pesos offset a liquidity shortage originally estimated at 4.837 billion pesos due to credit maturities.
Traders expected overnight rates to fall slightly in early trade on Tuesday, but expected upside pressure to continue due to liquidity pressure.
Credit maturities for Tuesday were estimated at 6.286 billion pesos.
